question: arXiv:2209.00006v2 compares the best-fit spectra of its Galactic Center excess candidates when each is fitted together with ring-based templates. Which candidate gives the faintest excess, and how good is its fit? What does the paper say about the spectra of the candidates that include the boxy bulge? And how does the dark matter spectrum obtained with the ring-based templates compare with those spectra and with the dark matter result obtained with the astrophysics-based templates of Cholis et al.?

arguments.answer:
The faintest excess comes from the X-shaped bulge. It is also the worst fit. With ring-based templates its −2ΔlnL is +30 relative to no excess, so it is slightly worse than having no excess. Its Δln B is −190.

Every excess that includes the boxy bulge has a very similar spectrum. This covers the boxy bulge alone, the boxy bulge "plus" (with the nuclear stellar bulge), and the boxy bulge together with the X-shaped bulge. The paper calls these spectra relatively soft and "compatible with having absorbed unmodeled diffuse flux".

The dark matter spectrum fitted with ring-based templates is harder on average than those bulge-type spectra. It is similar in spectrum to the dark matter result with the astrophysics-based templates of Cholis et al., but lower in flux. It also has "wiggles" between energy bins that neither dark matter annihilation nor millisecond pulsars predict.
